concept.title: The Projects page
concept.shortdesc: When you sign in, OpenV opens Home: the Projects page of the active workspace, which brings everything in it together. Home is at the top of the rail on every page.

ul.li: Along the top are the workspace's figures: how many artifacts its projects hold, the share of their requirements that are traced (a test case verifies them) and verified, and how many test cases fail.

Needs you lists what waits on you across every project, each line naming its project: artifacts in review to approve, suspect links to confirm, test runs in progress, failing test cases and new comments. The link on the right opens each one where it is dealt with.
Activity shows the newest events across the workspace's projects, who did what to which artifact. When agents have proposed changes, a card below it counts the proposals waiting.

Projects, below them, is where you pick a project. Each row shows the project's name and how many artifacts it holds, a one-line description, and two bars: the share of its requirements that are traced and the share verified. A project with no requirements yet says so instead. The project you opened last is marked with a blue edge. Each row carries its action buttons:

strow.stentry: Save as template — snapshot this project as a reusable template
Edit project — rename it or change the description
Download — opens the download wizard (format, sections, attachments)
Delete project — removes the project and all its artifacts

conbody.p: Click anywhere else on the row to open the project.
